ana_infra: FYI — forecast gap in GPU commitments for us-west next quarter. Demand curve spiking from hosted API; committed supply doesn't cover peak days. Need quick mitigation plan. :warning:

capacity_bot: [alert] Reserved utilization projection breach: us-west-a A100: commit=1200h/day, projected_demand=1850h/day, breach_days=12 (next 30d)

mike_finops: Can you share the numbers and the assumptions? is this peak traffic or sustained?

ana_infra: small typo — ana :) but here's the quick snapshot:
```
-- query: last-30d peak-day-profile (hosted api)
peak_day_gpu_hours (A100 equivalent): 1850
median_day_gpu_hours: 1100
reserved_commit: 1200
buffer (commit - median): +100
expected_breach_days: 10-15 (based on promo schedule + new PLG funnel)
```

sam_ops: ok, so we have ~650h/day of unmet peak demand on those 10-15 days. Rough monthly delta ~650*12 peak-days = ~7800h. Could we absorb with shared hosted pool bursts? what's current spare headroom across regions?

ana_infra: short answer: hosted shared pool has limited headroom atm — we've been using burst to handle small spikes but not sustained 600+h. Cross-region spare (eu-west + us-east) totals ~1200h/day but latency/cost tradeoffs for routing hosted customers.

lee_sre: latency for routing to eu-west for us-west customers will increase p50 ~25-40ms depending on model pathing; some SLAs allow it, others not. Also need to validate KV cache locality impact.

zara_product: we have two enterprise customers on contracts with stronger latency guarantees. Can't route their production traffic out of region without sign-off. We could route non-SLA hosted traffic and beta users.

mike_finops: Cost angle: if we buy short-term additional commitment (convert to reserved) it's 20-25% discount vs on-demand but requires commitment term. Alternatively, temporary on-demand bursts cost ~2.8x commit unit price. Rough calc: 7800h * on-demand premium ~ big $$. Do we have negotiation room with provider to shift some of our committed SKUs between regions?

ana_infra: negotiation is an option — cloud sales said region reallocation possible but non-trivial; may need region-specific commits or credits. Quick mitigations I'd propose: 1) enable prioritized routing to bursts for non-SLA hosted traffic, 2) enable model-routing to smaller quantized variants for low-critical routes, 3) activate cross-region overflow for gradable traffic, 4) start 60d negotiation with provider for partial commit reallocation, 5) immediate cost control: throttle experimental / internal-heavy pipelines during peak windows.

sam_ops: on (1) — we can tag routes as "best-effort-burst" and adjust smart routing policy within 24h. On (2) — need model owners to opt-in; can we auto-fallback to 4-bit quantized for non-sensitive customers?

ana_infra: yes, Redwood runtime supports per-route model variants and automatic fallback. Suggest default fallback to quantized-x4 for routes not flagged "latency-critical".

lee_sre: (3) cross-region overflow: requires checking egress limits and KV cache warm-start penalty. We'll prototype with a small traffic slice and measure p95 impact.

mike_finops: Action on negotiating commit reallocation — I'll start contact with cloud account rep today. Also will run quick TCO: buy extra commit (3-6 months) vs on-demand bursts. Need numbers by EOD Friday to present to ops leadership.

zara_product: I'll scrub the route list and mark which hosted customers are "latency-critical" vs safe-to-shift. ETA tomorrow noon.

ana_infra: Great. I'll own implementation of routing flags + quick policy to route "best-effort-burst" to shared pool or cross-region. ETA 48h for config + rollout in canary.

sam_ops: I'll prepare a short playbook and runbook for on-call if we flip routing during peak. Includes rollback steps, SLO checks, and dashboards to watch.

capacity_bot: [note] Action items recorded: negotiate_commit (mike_finops), route_flags (zara_product/ana), routing_impl (ana_infra), runbook (sam_ops), cross-region-proto (lee_sre).

mike_finops: Quick ask — can infra estimate the delta in unit-cost if we fallback 30% of hosted traffic to quantized models during peaks? even rough % token-cost drop helps our case.

ana_infra: ballpark: quantized variant reduces GPU processing time ~25-35% per token on our tests; combined with batching gains for lower-quality paths we might see ~30% unit cost reduction for those routes. I'll run a sim and post numbers tomorrow.

lee_sre: I'll schedule the prototype cross-region test for tomorrow 09:00 UTC against a subset of non-critical routes. Will post traffic plan and expected metrics.

zara_product: thx. one more: alert customers with upcoming feature promos (marketing) — PMs to coordinate so we avoid stacking promos across regions.

ana_infra: Summary of immediate next steps: (A) route flagging + canary rollout (ana/sam) 48h, (B) quick cost sim for quantized fallback (ana) by EOD tomorrow, (C) cloud negotiation kickoff (mike) today, (D) cross-region prototype (lee) tomorrow 09:00, (E) product customer list scrub (zara) noon tomorrow.

sam_ops: +1. I'll create the incident-lite channel for coordination and post the runbook link when ready. :spiral_calendar:  

mike_finops: Got it — will pull rough spend numbers and propose short-term commit buy vs sustained bursts.

ana_infra: Thanks all. If we can hit the canary and cost sim quickly we can avoid emergency capacity purchases. I'll post updates in this thread. :eyes:
